properties.title: TiO2 Abundance · Kaguya MI 65N-65S (Shi et al. 2026)
properties.authors: Shi X., Chen J., Wang J., Liu S., Tong X., Li J., Yan Z., Wen S., Xie H., He Z., Chu J., Hu W., Wang F.
properties.producer_institution_name: Tongji University; Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
properties.crs: Source: 9 GeoTIFFs of 20480 x 66560 px, geographic GCS_Moon_2000 in degrees on the 1737400 m sphere. COG: the 9 joined, IAU:30100, same sphere and grid.
properties.processing:lineage: Kaguya Multiband Imager level 5 reflectance after terrain shadow correction (8 bands, 415 to 1550 nm) and the spectral angles θTi and θFe, inverted with a residual 1D CNN (Res-CNN). Leave-one-out training on 56 samples from Apollo, Luna, Chang'E-5, and Chang'e-6 sites gives 56 models whose weights are averaged. Distributed as 9 Float32 GeoTIFFs of 40° longitude, 65N to 65S, 512 ppd, values in wt%, clipped to the product range. COG: gdalbuildvrt joins the 9 files (one grid, no resampling); gdal_calc.py maps the source NoData (3.4e38) to -9999; gdal_translate assigns IAU:30100 and writes a COG with DEFLATE/PREDICTOR=3 compression.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Higher TiO2 identifies ilmenite-rich mare basalt, a resource target for oxygen and iron extraction. 59 m/pixel between 65N and 65S.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Res-CNN TiO2 from Kaguya MI, calibrated with Chang'e-6 samples, 59 m/pixel, 65N-65S. RMSE 0.33 wt% at the training sites. Orbit stripes in places; NoData along orbit gaps; bands at 0 and 12 wt% along some gaps.
properties.lri:quality_note: RMSE 0.33 wt% between map and measured values at the 56 training sites; R² 0.98 and RMSE 1.99 wt% over the six oxides at held-out test sites (Supplementary Table 4). Pixel mean 0.94 wt%, equal to the article's global mean (0.94 wt%). Values are clipped to 0 to 12 wt% (15.66% of valid pixels at 0, 0.139% at 12). The pixels at 0 wt% cover most of the highlands, so highland TiO2 carries no gradient. Bands at 0 and 12 wt%, a few km wide, line some orbit gaps at 20 to 36°E and 59°E. NoData covers 1.53% of pixels, mostly in gaps along orbit tracks, and up to 21% of each column within 0.2° west and 0.4° east of 180°. North-south stripes about 1.06° apart, the longitude step between successive Kaguya orbits, appear at 20 to 35°E and 55 to 100°E and more weakly at 110 to 135°W and near 165°E; column means deviate from their 1° running median by up to 0.9 wt%. The source is 9 files of 40° longitude. At 180° the two sides do not match pixel for pixel (mean step -0.03 wt%); at 60°E the mean step is below 0.01 wt%; the other boundaries are continuous. Registered to the LRO frame: at 10 of 12 landing sites the offset to Speyerer et al. (2023) FeO, registered to the LROC WAC mosaic, is within 0.3 km.
